prs.title: Harden malformed metadata handling
prs.taskSummary:
## Summary

- Harden malformed metadata handling across type names, handles, signatures, IL disassembly, resources, and P/Invoke metadata.
- Keep `ilspycmd` and the decompiler alive when invalid rows, heap indices, tokens, or recursive metadata are encountered.
- Return safe fallback names or error markers instead of allowing malformed input to abort processing.

## Details

- Resolve TypeDef metadata by handle and tolerate invalid names and namespaces.
- Add safe fallbacks for malformed metadata handles, signatures, marshal descriptors, generic names, parameter sequences, and local-signature tokens.
- Contain invalid IL metadata during disassembly.
- Validate embedded resource payload bounds.
- Handle invalid inline-array field counts without `SingleOrDefault` failures.
- Preserve P/Invoke metadata when calling-convention bits are unknown.
- Bound recursive TypeDef, TypeRef, and ExportedType name resolution.

## Verification

- `OPENSSL_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES=1 pwsh ./build.ps1 -Configuration Debug --no-restore`
- `OPENSSL_ENABLE_SHA1_SIGNATURES=1 dotnet test --project ICSharpCode.Decompiler.Tests/ICSharpCode.Decompiler.Tests.csproj --no-build --report-trx`
- Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Tests: 3,742 passed, 49 skipped, 0 failed.
- Generated malformed fixtures and corpus sweeps completed without process failures.

prs.title: fix(routes): populate request.headers from incoming HTTP headers
prs.taskSummary:
`HttpRequestHandler._prepare_request` built a `base.Request` without ever copying `self.headers` into it, so `request.headers` was always `{}` in every route handler — breaking header-based auth, content negotiation, and CORS checks. ## Change - **`pyrevitlib/pyrevit/routes/server/server.py`** — after constructing `base.Request`, iterate `self.headers.items()` and call `request.add_header(key, value)` for each entry. Works on both IronPython 2 (`mimetools.Message`) and CPython 3 (`email.message.Message`). ```python @api.route("/echo/", methods=["GET"]) def echo(request): # request.headers now contains the actual HTTP headers auth = request.headers.get("Authorization") # e.g. "******" return routes.make_response(data={"headers": dict(request.headers)}) ``` - Fixes #3765
